canvas-01.description: Sheet 1 of the November 1927 Milford atlas covers the northwest end of the borough between the Delaware River and the steep slope above it, from the sheet's top edge south to Bridge Street. Two long parallel streets run down the left half of the sheet: Railroad Avenue beside the Belvidere Division of the Pennsylvania Railroad, with a footpath noted along its driveway, and Spring Garden, lined with scattered frame dwellings, hen houses, stables and a bicycle repair shop on deep lots that climb toward the slope. Spring Garden ends at Church, which runs east to Church Street Square, the short north-south street leading down to Bridge Street. The Milford Christian Church, a stone building heated by steam, stands at the head of Church Street Square. The south part of the sheet is the town centre on the north side of Bridge Street: the Gibson House hotel, the post office, a drug store, a paint store and dwellings with stores below, with Race Street meeting Bridge Street from the south at the bottom edge. A drive and a lane on the east side lead toward the foot of a steep hill and a creek at the right edge, where a driveway and a small bridge marked Tr. Bridge are drawn. At the lower left the covered wooden toll bridge to Pennsylvania leaves Bridge Street across the river, with a private pump house and a fire water pipe on the river bank. The upper right of the sheet carries the title, the specials index, the water facilities and fire department notes and a key map at 600 feet to an inch, all outside this part's mask, and a key to the symbols at top centre, also masked out. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Race Street is today's Carpenter Street (OpenStreetMap).
Church Street Square is today the north-south leg of Church Street; the east-west Church is also Church Street.
Railroad Avenue north of Bridge Street, west of the railroad, has no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap; today's Railroad Avenue starts at Bridge Street and runs south-east.
Spring Garden north of Church was found displaced against the modern Spring Garden Street in the 1912 edition; not used for control here.
Ways lettered only Drive, Lane and Driveway at the east side of the sheet are not named streets.
The railroad (Belvidere Division, Pennsylvania Railroad) is disused or abandoned today.

Printed sheet 1 (canvas labelled Index), 50 ft. Map of Church Street Square, Spring Garden Street, Railroad Avenue and Church Street down to Bridge Street; the upper right carries the index, key map at 600 ft, title cartouche, water facilities, and a key legend at top centre, all masked out. New for 1927 (milford-1912 had no 1927 sheet 1).

sheet-2-1.description: The right-hand part of sheet 2 shows the north end of Milford on both sides of the Quequacommissicong Creek, drawn at a slightly different angle from the left part of the sheet and separated from it by a heavy stepped line. North of the creek, Water Street runs up the left side between the creek and the head race of the W. & W. E. Thomas feed and grist mill, which stands on the race with its office and a wagon shed; the mill is noted as not in operation except to pump water to the city reservoir. York runs north-east from Water Street to meet Mill, and continues north-east toward the top right corner, lined on its east side by frame dwellings on narrow lots numbered from 101 upward. Mill crosses the creek on an iron bridge, and a second iron bridge carries Water Street over the creek further west. South of the creek the part shows Water Street and Mill running south through a residential block, with Private Street, a short private way, between them, and dwellings, stables and sheds on both frontages. A six-inch water main from the stand pipe is drawn along Mill and across to Water Street. The bottom of this part continues onto the top of the left part of the same sheet, where both streets reach Quequa Street; hydrants and street widths (40 feet on Water Street, 30 feet on Mill) are repeated on both parts. Open ground with no exposure lies along the right edge. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch, at a scale about 3 percent smaller than the rest of the atlas by the fit.
notes: York north-east of Mill is today York Road; between Water and Mill it is York Street (OpenStreetMap).
Private Street is not in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from one detected junction (Mill / York Road / York Street), one hand-picked junction (Water / York) and two hydrants carried from part 2 of the same sheet.

Sheet 2, 50 ft, two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 right (Water, Mill and York Streets north and south of the creek, W. & W. E. Thomas mill), part 2 left (Water Street from Bridge to Quequa, Frenchtown Road). Same scan as milford-1912 canvas-03 (skipped there).

sheet-2-2.description: The left-hand part of sheet 2 shows the main north-south street of Milford, Water Street, from Bridge Street north to Quequa Street, with the Quequacommissicong Creek along the left edge. Water Street is lined with the town's older commercial and residential buildings: the Milford House hotel with a pool room and bar, a harness shop, Samuel Raub's carriage shop with its wheelwright and carriage painting shop, a slaughter house on the creek bank, stores and dwellings. Mill branches north-east from Water Street at a long fork near the fire department building and fire alarm, and runs past the Catholic Church to Quequa Street at the top of the part. At the south end, Bridge Street comes in from the iron bridge over the creek and meets Water Street and Frenchtown Road, which runs south-east past the Presbyterian Church and its church sheds, a garage for about 25 cars, and dwellings; a short lane loops off Frenchtown Road to the east. A fire alarm box for the railroad locomotive tire is marked by the iron bridge, and a six-inch water main runs along Water Street and down Frenchtown Road. The right side of this part, east of the Water Street lots, is mostly open ground with a few outbuildings. The top of this part continues from the bottom of the right-hand part of the same sheet. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Quequa is today's Pine Street (OpenStreetMap).
The fork of Mill from Water Street is long and sharp, with no defined centre; that junction was not used for control.
Bridge Street / Frenchtown Road / Water Street was hand-picked at the drawn centrelines; the detector placed it 17 ft north.

Sheet 2, 50 ft, two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 right (Water, Mill and York Streets north and south of the creek, W. & W. E. Thomas mill), part 2 left (Water Street from Bridge to Quequa, Frenchtown Road). Same scan as milford-1912 canvas-03 (skipped there).

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 covers the business row on the south side of Bridge Street and the grid of streets south of it between the Delaware River and the Quequacommissicong Creek. Along Bridge Street stand the First National Bank, the I.O.O.F. hall, a printing office, a bakery and brick stores with dwellings above, backing onto the head race that runs east to west behind them. West of these the Pennsylvania Railroad (Belvidere Division) runs down the sheet with its passenger station, freight house, a long passing siding, coal and lumber sheds, a building material warehouse, a hand car tool house and the Kinney and Smith feed store. On the river bank at the top left is the Little, Wilson and Deats Milford Mill, a flour mill with a feed and grain storehouse. East of the railroad, Railroad Avenue and Race run south and are crossed by Green, Maple and Orchard, with frame dwellings on regular lots, the opera house with a lodge hall on Race, and the Henry Hauptfuhrer creamery beside the railroad at the bottom. Church Street and a drive are drawn at the top edge north of Bridge Street, and Race reaches the creek bank on the east, where open ground slopes down to the creek. A six-inch main runs along Bridge Street and four-inch pipes along the cross streets. The lower left corner holds a separate inset of the public school, which is its own part. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Race is today's Carpenter Street (OpenStreetMap).

Railroad Avenue is drawn with its west side open to railroad land; its four junctions were hand-picked as the drawn east edge plus 12 ft (half the modern right-of-way), because the detector paired rails or lot lines 10 to 40 ft west.
Bridge / Race was hand-picked: the detector paired a building line 22 ft east.
The railroad is disused or abandoned today.

Sheet 3, 50 ft, two parts: part 1 main (Bridge Street row, Railroad Avenue, Race Street, Green, Maple, Orchard, railroad yard, Milford Mill), part 2 inset bottom left (Milford Public School at Frenchtown Road and Mt. Pleasant Road). Same scan as milford-1912 sheet-3 (skipped there).

sheet-3-2.description: A small inset in the lower left corner of sheet 3, enclosed by heavy lines, shows the Milford Public School on its own at the edge of town. The school is a two-storey brick building of irregular plan, heated by steam and lit by electricity, standing on a large lot marked 57 between Frenchtown Road, which runs along the lower left edge of the inset, and Mt. Pleasant Road, which curves across the bottom. The two roads meet just beyond the lower left corner of the inset. A steep hill is noted on the east side of the lot, and a note at the left gives the distance to a two-storey frame dwelling outside the inset. The inset has its own north arrow, turned about the same as the main part of the sheet, and is drawn at the sheet's scale of 50 feet to an inch. Nothing else is drawn in the inset; the rest of it is open ground.
notes: Mt. Pleasant Road is today's Milford - Mount Pleasant Road (OpenStreetMap).
Placed from a single hand-picked point, the meeting of the drawn road centrelines just off the inset corner, with the scale and rotation of the main part: low confidence.
